title: Decision Entropy Prioritizer: integrating uncertainty into token-econ + latency scoring
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: Traditional RICE-style prioritization at Redwood favors high-reach / high-impact items but underweights the value of reducing model or routing uncertainty. For inference roadmap decisions we frequently face initiatives that decrease unit cost at the expense of increased latency variance, or that unlock predictable capacity but with uncertain quality regressions.

Proposal: Introduce a Decision Entropy Prioritizer (DEP) — a scoring component that augments RICE by penalizing (or rewarding) initiatives based on the expected reduction in decision entropy (uncertainty about outcome distributions) and by explicitly applying a latency-regime penalty. The goal is to surface work that simultaneously improves token economics and reduces delivery risk for downstream product teams.

Scoring formula (high-level):
DEP_score = (Adjusted_Reach * Confidence * Impact) / (Effort + LatencyPenalty + CostDelta) - k * ResidualEntropy
Where:
- Adjusted_Reach = Reach * (1 - overlap_with_existing_initiatives)
- Confidence = Historical success rate for similar initiative cohorts (0.0-1.0)
- Impact = normalized customer/business value (1-10)
- Effort = estimated points converted to normalized cost units
- LatencyPenalty = penalty function that scales with expected p95 latency increase (or rewards p95 reduction)
- CostDelta = expected delta in $/token or $/throughput
- ResidualEntropy = measured remaining uncertainty after the initiative (bits)
- k = calibrated tradeoff coefficient (product policy)

Operationalization:
1) Define a schema for Confidence and ResidualEntropy estimations (see Acceptance Criteria).
2) Add a prioritization UI layer to the roadmap tool that shows standard RICE fields plus DEP components and a final normalized score.
3) Calibrate k using historical closed initiatives (retro-simulation across last 12 months).
4) Run a pilot for Cycle 12: grade 12 candidate initiatives using both classic RICE and DEP, compare selected set and estimate projected token-econ + latency risk reduction.

Why different from existing frameworks: DEP explicitly encodes uncertainty reduction as first-class; it penalizes initiatives that look attractive on expected impact but leave large unknowns (e.g., experimental kernel swaps, aggressive quantization without eval sets). It encourages investments in observability, eval suites, and smaller de-risking experiments that reduce platform decision entropy over time.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Schema documented: confidence and residual entropy defined with examples and scoring rubric.
2) Pilot dataset prepared: 12 past initiatives mapped to DEP inputs for calibration.
3) Roadmap UI mock with DEP fields reviewed by PM + Eng + Design.
4) Calibration run completed and recommended k provided.
5) Pilot selection run (Cycle 12) produces a ranked list; retrospective shows improved clarity on tradeoffs (qualitative reviews from 3 partner PMs).

2026-03-11 Mateo Alvarez: Agreed to lead calibration. Recommended we include kernel-level variance metrics and KV-cache hit-rate variance in ResidualEntropy inputs.

2026-03-12 Lina Park (Research): Shared a CSV of 18 prior initiatives with success_rate, p95_latency_change, cost_delta, and outcome_variance. Starting retro-sim this week. Link: https://redwood.intra/drive/dep-dataset-2026
2026-03-13 Jordan Park (Design): Drafted a compact UI pattern (table + sparklines) that shows ResidualEntropy and LatencyPenalty as small badges. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/dep-ui

2026-03-14 Mateo Alvarez: Added engineering constraints in comment thread — need runtime telemetry hooks for p95 estimates and an eval harness to measure quality-variance for model-change initiatives. Blocking: infra task ENG-19422 (telemetry: p95 sampling hooks) — recommended dependency.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: 1) A larger k promotes lower-variance investments (observability/experiments) but risks starving big bet features; propose decay schedule for k across quarters. 2) ResidualEntropy estimation is noisy for novel model ops; require minimum confidence threshold to avoid junk scoring.

Plan: calibration (2 weeks) -> UI proto + API for scoring (3 weeks) -> Pilot run in Cycle 12. If pilot signals improved decision alignment, fold DEP into quarterly roadmap reviews as a secondary score alongside RICE.
